page.overview:
What is Easterlings?

Easterlings, also known as the Hróatani, the Rhúnedain,

As of the Third Age, Easterlings were a people diverse in height and skin tone. Their skin was either sallow or olive, their eyes were dark (dark brown and black), and their straight hair was black. One unique variant appeared at the Siege of Gondor, described as broad, short, bearded, and wielding axes. It is unspecified, although likely, that the Easterlings of the First Age (told of in the Quenta Silmarillion) were the primary ancestors of those that later settled Rhûn.

In the late First Age, Men awoke in Hildórien in the East. Early on, some of them were corrupted by Morgoth, prompting others, such as the Edain, to migrate westwards.

In the year 463, some tribes of Men joined the Edain in Beleriand after the Dagor Bragollach passing north around the Ered Luin and into Lothlann, having heard the rumor of its land and riches while others were secretly in league with Morgoth. Some folk remained in Eriador. These Easterlings were called Eastrons, and the two greatest chieftains amongst them were Bór and Ulfang. Bór's sons were Borlach, Borlad, and Borthand. Bór and his sons swore allegiance to Maedhros, and remained faithful, even though he had been ordered by Morgoth to betray the banner of Caranthir. All of them were slain in the Nírnaeth Arnoediad.
